title: Pressure-cooker shredded chicken
subtitle: Tender, pullable chicken in 8 minutes
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs cooked under pressure until they shred easily. A versatile base for tacos, sandwiches, salads, or pasta, season plainly to use across multiple dishes.
sourceNotes: Poaching and shredding chicken is a technique common to many cuisines, in Mexico as tinga base, in China as the starting point for cold salads, in the UK as the basis for pies and pasta. The pressure-cooker version compresses poaching time from 25 minutes to 8.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, then freeze in airtight bags or containers for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half. Shredded chicken defrosts quickly and is ready to use from cold.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and shred up to 3 days ahead. Store refrigerated with a little of the cooking liquid to keep it moist.

content.text: Pressure-cooker shredded chicken is a meal-prep staple. Boneless thighs cooked with stock and aromatics for 8 minutes at high pressure come out completely tender, pulling apart into long, juicy strands with two forks. It is the kind of thing you make once and use across three or four meals across the week.

Season the chicken plainly, salt, pepper, garlic, a bay leaf, so the result is versatile. You can dress it with barbecue sauce for tacos, toss it with mayonnaise for sandwiches, fold it into pasta with cream, or add it to a soup at the end. Heavily seasoned shredded chicken at this stage is too committed; neutral chicken can go anywhere.
Reserve the cooking liquid. It is a light chicken broth that can be used as stock for soups or to moisten the shredded meat before storing.

Put the chicken thighs into the pressure cooker. Add {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock, the bruised garlic cloves, the bay leaf, and salt and pepper. The liquid should come at least halfway up the chicken, add a little water if needed.
Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 8 minutes. Allow a natural pressure release of 5 minutes, then quick-release any remaining pressure.

Lift the chicken thighs out of the cooking liquid and onto a board. Use two forks to pull the meat apart into shreds, it should come apart with almost no effort. Taste and season. Reserve the cooking liquid separately as a light stock. Use the shredded chicken immediately or store in a container with a splash of the cooking liquid to keep it moist.

rows.symptom: The chicken is tough and does not shred easily
rows.cause: Insufficient cooking time, or the thighs were very large.
rows.fix: Return the chicken to the sealed pot and cook at high pressure for a further 5 minutes. At 8 minutes, thighs should be fully cooked; at 12 to 15 minutes, they will shred completely.

rows.cause: The thighs were skinless breast meat, which dries out under pressure, or there was insufficient liquid.
rows.fix: Toss the shredded meat immediately with a few tablespoons of the cooking liquid. For next time, use bone-in or skin-on thighs, which are more forgiving under pressure.

rows.cause: The aromatics were too minimal to flavour a full batch.
rows.fix: Add an extra clove of garlic, a sprig of thyme, and a carrot next time. The liquid becomes a usable light stock, season it before using.

content.text: Shredded chicken freezes well. Cool completely, portion into zip-lock bags or containers, and freeze for up to 3 months. Include a splash of the cooking liquid in each portion. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a pan with a little liquid, or use cold in salads and wraps.

Shredded chicken is less a dish than a building block. A Sunday afternoon batch translates into a Monday pasta, a Tuesday sandwich, and a Wednesday soup without any extra cooking. The pressure cooker makes the basic component faster than any other method and produces a better result than baked or pan-fried chicken intended for shredding, the moist, even heat of the sealed pot does not dry the meat out.
